facts.statement: The genus was first found in the 1960s but was not recognized as a crocodyliform until 1995, when it was initially mistaken for a multituberculate mammal.
facts.quote: Chimaerasuchus was originally discovered in the 1960s but not identified as a crocodyliform until 1995, instead thought to possibly be a multituberculate mammal.

facts.statement: The genus name Chimaerasuchus translates to "chimera crocodile".
facts.quote: Chimaerasuchus ("chimera crocodile") is an extinct genus of Chinese crocodyliform from the Early Cretaceous Wulong Formation.

facts.statement: Four teeth at the tip of its short snout gave the animal a distinctive "bucktoothed" look.
facts.quote: The four teeth in the very tip of its short snout gave it a "bucktoothed" appearance.

facts.statement: Its multicusped and varied teeth suggest it was an herbivore, a trait that evolved multiple times in Mesozoic crocodyliforms.
facts.quote: Due its multicusped teeth and marked heterodonty, it is believed to have been an herbivore: an adaptation which evolved numerous times across Mesozoic crocodyliforms.

facts.statement: The animal was small, estimated to be about 1 meter in length, and lightly built.
facts.quote: It was not a particularly large animal, estimated to be around 1 m long and not very heavily built.

facts.statement: Its short forelimbs ended in sharp, highly curved claws.
facts.quote: Its forelimbs were short but had sharp and highly curved claws.

facts.statement: The snout measured approximately 65 mm and the total skull length was around 135 mm, resulting in a very short jaw compared to other crocodyliforms.
facts.quote: It is thought that the snout reached 65 mm and the entire skull was around 135 mm long, giving Chimaerasuchus a very short jaw and mouth compared with other crocodyliforms.

facts.statement: The maxillary teeth were unusual, resembling mammalian molars or premolars rather than typical crocodyliform teeth, and were broad and suited for grinding.
facts.quote: The maxillary teeth are very unusual, as they more closely resemble molars or premolars from a mammal than normal crocodyliform teeth, as they are large and broad, more suited to grinding than slicing.

facts.statement: A ridge on the outside of the mandible may have supported soft cheek tissue to prevent plant matter from escaping while chewing, similar to Notosuchus.
facts.quote: A ridge extends along the external side of the mandible, which may have been for the attachment of soft cheek tissue to prevent plant matter escaping while being chewed as in Notosuchus.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence includes three cervical and twelve dorsal vertebrae, though none are in good condition.
facts.quote: Three cervical and twelve dorsal vertebrae are preserved, although none are in good condition.

facts.statement: The preserved vertebrae were amphicoelous, had low neural spines, and possessed large neural canals in the cervical region.
facts.quote: Those that have reasonably-preserved centra show that these were amphicoelous, The neural spines are low, but the neural canals are quite large in all the cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: One incomplete osteoderm was preserved, featuring a sculpted surface and a small ventral peg.
facts.quote: One osteoderm is preserved, and it is incomplete, but it is partially sculpted and has a small ventral peg.

facts.statement: The extent of the animal's dermal armour remains unknown.
facts.quote: It is unknown how extensive the dermal armour was.

facts.statement: The humeri were about 82 mm long and the ulnae about 76 mm long, contributing to its short front legs.
facts.quote: The humeri are estimated to be about 82 mm long and the ulnae to be 76 mm long, giving Chimaerasuchus rather short front legs.

facts.statement: The likely phalangeal formula was 2, 3, 3, 4, 3, including strongly curved and arched unguals.
facts.quote: The phalangeal formula is probably 2, 3, 3, 4, 3 (including the unguals, which are strongly curved and arched).

facts.statement: The ischium was narrow and elongated, a feature more pronounced than in almost any other crocodyliform.
facts.quote: The ischium is narrow and elongated, more so than almost any other crocodyliform.

facts.statement: The genus was described by Wu et al. in 1995.
facts.quote: authority: Wu et al., 1995

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Chimaerasuchus paradoxus.
facts.quote: type_species: Chimaerasuchus paradoxus

facts.statement: Chimaerasuchus belongs to the parent group Ziphosuchia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ziphosuchia

facts.statement: The animal is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The species lived from the Aptian to the Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)
